A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same regularized personalized federated learning work despite substantial renaming and restructuring. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original synthetic logistic-regression simulations and experiments on MNIST, EMNIST, and CIFAR10, including appendix comparisons and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains original empirical results and adds linear-regression experiments, dynamic-personalization results, and CelebA and Sent140 evaluations.

M1.justification: The regularized objective and warm-start K-step algorithm remain. V4 adds a validation-triggered strategy that increases λ during training (Section 6.2/Figure 3), whereas v3 selected λ according to heterogeneity. Algorithm 2 formalizes mini-batch SGD, but SGD was already documented for v3's real-data experiments.

E1.justification: V4 adds overdetermined synthetic linear regression and naturally partitioned CelebA and Sent140 experiments, expanding task coverage and client-data scenarios. Synthetic logistic regression, MNIST, EMNIST, and CIFAR10 remain.

E2.justification: The evaluated Dichotomous Strategy is removed with v3's Table 4 and Appendix C.3. V4 also includes pFedMe in the MNIST-Logit comparison in Table 4; v3's corresponding plots compared against LocalTrain and GlobalTrain. The pFedMe CNN comparisons were already present.

E3.justification: New protocols include condition-number sweeps using theory-prescribed step sizes and local-update budgets, with optimization error evaluated against communication rounds and gradient evaluations (Figures 7–8), and validation-triggered λ tuning (Figure 3). The dichotomous sample-splitting/model-selection protocol disappears. Existing classification hyperparameters and the 100/1,000-client, 10% sampling design remain.

E4.justification: V4 adds analyses of how conditioning affects communication and computation, and whether dynamic personalization can approach favorable accuracy–communication choices. V3's Figure 3 analysis of heterogeneity-adaptive λ and its supplementary CNN local-update analysis disappear. The client-count scalability analysis is retained as v4 Figure 6.

E5.justification: Both retain the same 20/50 'total runs' disclosures for existing real-data experiments. Neither adds seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or empirical error bars. V4's stochastic-noise bounds concern theory rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V4 adds dynamic-λ and condition-number results, MNIST-Logit table entries, and CelebA/Sent140 losses and accuracies. Figures 9–10 report low-personalization FedCLUP accuracies of 0.919 and 0.734, respectively, without v3 counterparts. Dichotomous-strategy and adaptive-λ statistical-error results are removed. Existing CNN table scores remain, including MNIST-CNN2 accuracy 0.9032 at large λ/low personalization.

T1.justification: The earlier tuned-λ minimax result survives as Corollary 1 and Appendix A.4. V4 adds Theorem 1's explicit λ-dependent bound, the combined statistical/optimization bound in Corollary 3, and stochastic assumptions, lemmas, and Theorem 3 in Appendix B.5. Strong convexity changes from the individual loss to empirical risk. Appendix C gives a different contraction factor from the main trade-off corollary.

C1.justification: V3 foregrounds minimax statistical accuracy for FedProx and the communication–computation trade-off. V4 makes quantitative statistical accuracy–communication characterization the central contribution, adds stochastic-efficiency claims, and explicitly presents minimax optimality as a side contribution in the abstract.

C2.justification: V4 adds guidance for balancing statistical and optimization errors at a target accuracy and explains LocalTrain's poor table results through evaluation on unseen classes. The dichotomous-strategy interpretation is removed. Its rewritten Figure 2 discussion also reverses v3's personalization–communication interpretation, conflicting with v4's own theoretical discussion and conclusion.

D1.justification: V4 supplies explicit mini-batch sampling pseudocode, regularization values and preprocessing references for CelebA/Sent140, and clarifies whole-dataset evaluation. The code-access reference changes from an anonymous hosting address to a GitHub repository. Most existing learning rates, batch sizes, epochs, and architecture descriptions are retained.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts from a FedProx-focused minimax analysis to an algorithm-independent PFL accuracy–communication analysis. V4 adds distinctions from Bietti et al.'s privacy trade-off and newer optimization literature, and expands application references. The theoretical comparison replaces Ditto with AL2SGD and adds statistical-error coverage; these are literature comparisons, not new empirical baselines.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Statistical and optimization analyses are grouped under Section 4, a dedicated trade-off section is introduced, and appendix material is reorganized. V4 also removes the duplicated reference list and adds acknowledgment and impact sections.

P2.justification: V4 changes the main text from single-column to two-column layout, reorganizes and relabels error plots, and summarizes selected appendix results in main-text Table 2. It adds dynamic-tuning, conditioning, and natural-partition figures, revises theoretical comparison tables, and removes the dichotomous comparison display.

improvement.justification: V4 broadens the theoretical analysis and adds useful empirical coverage, including strongly convex and naturally partitioned settings. However, the new central trade-off bound has unreconciled contraction factors in Equation (15) and Appendix C, Equation (157), while the Figure 2 discussion reverses the personalization–communication relationship stated correctly in v3. These issues affect the new central contribution, preventing a reliable judgment that the additions produce a net quality improvement.
